# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can operate only the three cut positions, and my touch view provides no distinguishing wire details yet. I should tell Mute that I need the manual-derived cut instruction, while waiting to hear Deaf’s spoken description next round.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can cut wire positions 1, 2, or 3. My touch view shows no distinguishing details. Please determine and relay the required cut position from the manual and Deaf's information.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb view: display reads 0. Light is blue. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

Deaf reports display 0, a blue light, and wires ordered red, yellow, blue. Mute needs this visible-bomb information to apply the manual and tell me which position to cut.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light blue; wires: position 1 red, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue. Please apply the manual and tell me exactly which position to cut.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is orange; display remains 0; wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured: ?.

The light has changed to orange. I cannot interpret Mute’s gesture because I cannot see gestures, and Mute cannot speak. Mute must convey the manual result to Deaf by gesture, then Deaf can say the cut position aloud to me. I should ensure Mute has the updated bomb state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Update from Deaf: display 0; light is now orange; wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I cannot see your gesture. Please gesture the manual's required cut position to Deaf, and have Deaf speak that position to me.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is yellow; display 0; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute again gestured: ?.

The current light is yellow. Mute’s gesture still cannot reach me visually, so the result must be relayed through Deaf’s voice. I will ask Mute to use an unmistakable position signal that Deaf can identify and announce aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I cannot see gestures. If the manual selects wire 1, 2, or 3, gesture that number plainly to Deaf (for example one/two/three raised fingers). Deaf: please say the indicated wire number aloud immediately so I can cut it.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: light is red; display 0; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute has gestured ? on each of the last three turns.

The light is now red, so any manual rule may depend on that current state. Mute’s prior gestures are inaccessible to me, but Deaf can see them; we need a stable visible code that Deaf can relay aloud. I will tell Mute to encode the selected position as familiar finger-number signs, and show Deaf those signs as the intended position code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state is display 0, red light, wires 1 red / 2 yellow / 3 blue. Use the manual for this current state. Encode the required cut position visibly as: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. Deaf should identify that sign and say its wire number aloud.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","✌","🤟"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current view: green light, display 0, wires 1 red 2 yellow 3 blue. Mute again gestured ?.

The light is now green. Mute receives my words, while Deaf receives only visible gestures, so Mute must send the answer as a conventional finger-number sign that Deaf can relay aloud. I will repeat the current state to Mute and show Deaf the three-number code again.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="New current state: display 0; GREEN light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Apply the manual to this state, then on your next turn gesture exactly: ☝ if cut 1, ✌ if cut 2, or 🤟 if cut 3. Deaf can see it and must say the number aloud.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","✌","🤟"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current view: blue light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute again made the same single gesture as before.

The current visible state is blue light, display 0, and red/yellow/blue wires. The persistent gesture cannot reach me directly. I will replace the ambiguous sign with a countable protocol: Mute should make one, two, or three consecutive thumbs-up gestures for wire 1, 2, or 3. Deaf can count them and say the count aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0, BLUE light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Ignore earlier gesture code. Apply the manual, then signal the answer as consecutive 👍 gestures: one 👍 means cut wire 1; two 👍 means wire 2; three 👍 means wire 3. Deaf, count them and say the count aloud.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👍","👍"])
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current view: orange light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The light is orange again, with display 0 and wires red/yellow/blue. No interpretable answer has yet been relayed. I will ask Mute to use a repeated, countable gesture code for the manual’s answer for this exact current state; Deaf can count the visible gestures and report the number vocally.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="State now: display 0; ORANGE light; wire 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Consult the manual for this exact state. Reply next turn with only repeated 👍: 1 👍 = cut wire 1; 2 👍 = wire 2; 3 👍 = wire 3. Deaf, please count Mute's 👍 and say the number aloud to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👍","👍"])
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current view: yellow light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The yellow-state instruction must be encoded in a way Deaf can recognize and voice. I will keep the countable thumbs-up protocol and wait for Deaf’s relay rather than cutting without a confirmed number.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the YELLOW-light state (display 0; wires red, yellow, blue), send only the answer as repeated 👍: one = cut 1, two = cut 2, three = cut 3. Deaf must count and say the number aloud.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👍","👍"])
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current view: red light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured ? ?.

Mute has now made two gesture symbols, likely the two-thumbs-up response requested for the earlier yellow-light state. That would encode wire 2, but the light is currently red, so I must not act on a response calculated for yellow. I need establish the count code visibly to Deaf: one thumbs-up maps to one, two to two, and three to three. Then Deaf can voice future counts. I will also send Mute the current red state for a fresh manual lookup.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0; RED light; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Use the manual for RED and reply with repeated 👍: 1 means wire 1, 2 means wire 2, 3 means wire 3. Do not change the code.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍","✌","👍","👍","🤟","👍","👍","👍"])
```

Deaf says to Blind: Current view: green light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The light is now green. I still have no voiced cut instruction. Mute’s prior signals were not relayed in a usable form, so I need Mute to make a clearly countable, conventional finger-number gesture for the current green state, which Deaf can identify and announce aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state is GREEN light, display 0, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Recheck the manual for this exact state. Signal only with a conventional count: ☝ for cut 1, ✌ for cut 2, or three raised fingers for cut 3. Deaf: describe the visible count aloud as wire 1, 2, or 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","✌","🤟"])
```

Mute’s two repeated gestures follow the count protocol I gave: two signals mean wire 2. The bomb state has changed since the request, but Mute has repeatedly returned the same two-signal answer, so wire 2 is the only manual-derived instruction available and is consistent across the reports. I will cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
